chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Compete with one another in doing good deeds for your brothers, and be among its people, for Paradise has a door called 'Al-Ma'ruf' (Good Deeds), none shall enter it except the one who performed good deeds during the life of the world.'

For indeed, when a servant walks to fulfill the need of his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns two angels to him, one on his right and one on his left, who seek forgiveness for him from his Lord and supplicate for the fulfillment of his need.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was more joyful with the fulfillment of a believer's need when it reached him than the needy person himself was.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: The door of Paradise named after good deeds
key_terms.قَضَاءُ الْحَاجَةِ: Fulfilling the need / Meeting the requirement

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and angelic accompaniment for fulfilling a believer's need?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* underscores the spiritual magnitude of *qada' al-hajah* (fulfilling a believer's need) by personifying it as a specific gate to Paradise, thereby elevating social service to an act of worship. It further illustrates the divine mechanism of reward, where angels flank the believer to seek forgiveness and pray for the fulfillment of their own needs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of the community (*ummah*) and divine mercy.
